# Slice fleet generation 2: raw qemu, per-VM kernel networking, trixie boxes, and network-abuse observability

## Overview

This spec defines the second generation of the imbue_cloud bare-metal slice fleet, replacing lima with directly-managed qemu and giving every slice VM its own kernel-visible network attachment.
It is the response to the 2026-08 SSH-storm incident and its follow-up issues: per-VM network abuse detection and enforcement (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#548) and the unhardened, internet-exposed box management sshd (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#549).

The key decisions:

- **Replace lima with raw qemu + systemd for slices.**
  Lima's design center is single-user dev laptops, and nearly every slice incident traces to it: per-boot cloud-init replay (the adoption-reconciler and key-repair machinery exist solely to fight it), the guestagent FD leak and its fleet-wide upgrade, the bundled-containerd conflict, start deadlines, and no path to tap networking or qemu flag control on Linux.
  A dev-box spike proved the replacement end to end: a VM booted from the production-staged base image under raw qemu with one-time cloud-init, a routed tap, nftables DNAT/SNAT, working egress, per-VM counters, clean QMP shutdown, and a byte-identical SSH host key across reboots (no cloud-init replay).
- **Per-VM routed-tap networking.**
  Each VM gets its own tap interface with a private /30 (no shared L2 segment, so no tenant-to-tenant ARP surface), the box routes and NATs, and the public contract (box IP + two forwarded ports) is preserved via kernel DNAT.
  This makes conntrack, tc, and nftables counters cleanly per-tenant, replaces lima's userspace hostagent/guestagent forwarding path with kernel NAT, and closes the incident's vector (guests have no route to the box's management plane).
- **Generation determines everything.**
  New boxes are ordered or repaved as generation 2 (Debian 13 "trixie" box OS, trixie slice guest image, XFS storage partition, the qemu backend, the management-plane lockdown); generation 1 boxes stay exactly as they are until drained and repaved.
  An integer `box_generation` column drives all dispatch; there are exactly two fleet states, never a matrix.
- **Fleet turnover by drain and repave, seeded by new orders.**
  Two fresh gen-2 boxes per production region (and one for staging) seed capacity; existing boxes are then drained (silent force-stop; restores land on gen-2) and repaved in batches.
  Workspaces migrate through the existing stop/start machinery, with the restore converting the artifact to the qemu layout and dist-upgrading the guest to trixie.
- **Management-plane lockdown (gen-2 only).**
  Box `:22` becomes default-drop, allowing only the connector's Modal Proxy static IPs; operators reach boxes over plain self-hosted WireGuard (peer list in a committed per-tier file).
- **Network-abuse telemetry and enforcement, alert-first.**
  Per-tap interface counters flow through the existing otelcol hostmetrics pipeline for free; a small collector emits per-VM nftables counters as journald JSON into the same pipeline; OpenObserve alert rules file GitHub issues (with SMTP to infra@imbue.com as the backup channel).
  Day-one enforcement is limited to rules no legitimate workspace ever hits: the ceilings (50,000 concurrent connections, 300 new connections/sec sustained, fair-share bandwidth), the management-plane block, an anti-spoofing drop (only the VM's own /30 address may leave its tap -- reflection/amplification participation is structurally impossible), and a direct-to-MX SMTP block (outbound TCP 25 dropped into a per-VM counter; authenticated submission via 587/465 stays open -- every tenant shares the box's masqueraded public IP, so one spammer would poison it for the whole box and draw OVH abuse action). Finer rules start alert-only and are promoted per-rule once their alert history is clean.
- **Hardening that lima blocked comes with the backend.**
  Each qemu runs as its own per-slice unix user (a VM escape lands in an account that owns only that VM), with qemu's `-sandbox` seccomp flags enabled (possible under systemd because there is no `-daemonize`).
  The unit additionally confines qemu with systemd's sandbox (`ProtectSystem=strict` with write access to only its QMP socket dir and its two disk images, `DevicePolicy=closed` allowing exactly `/dev/kvm` and `/dev/net/tun`, `SystemCallFilter=@system-service ~@privileged @resources`, `MemoryDenyWriteExecute`, `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX`, `IPAddressDeny=any`, the `Protect*` set -- `systemd-analyze security` 9.2 -> 1.0), runs qemu with `-nodefaults -no-user-config`, hides nested virtualization from the guest (`-cpu host,vmx=off,svm=off`, plus `kvm nested=0` at the box's module level), removes USB/SMM/S3/S4, attaches the cidata as a read-only virtio-blk disk, and routes the guest console to journald instead of an unbounded log file; the root helper pins `MemoryMax`/`CPUWeight`/`IOWeight`/`TasksMax` from the machine's size at every start (`MemoryMax` is a backstop whose firing is the `SLICE_UNIT_OOM_KILLED` telemetry signal).
  The workspace container inside the guest runs under gVisor (`runsc`, netstack, `--overlay2=none`, `/run` and `/tmp` on tmpfs) from the bake; the runtime ships in the gen-2 guest image (see `blueprint/slice-fleet-cutover/`). Volumes keep gVisor's default `shared` file access (no sentry-side metadata/page cache: an `exclusive` cache was measured and rejected because it lets a live btrfs snapshot see stale data), and machines are sized with `DEFAULT_SLICE_CPU_OVERCOMMIT_RATIO = 4.0` (4 vCPUs per 8 units) so the systrap sentry threads have room next to the application; both decided from the 2026-08-27 tuning pass. The guest's disks: a 10 GiB boot disk (OS + capped journal) and a quota-enabled btrfs data disk holding docker's data-root, the workspace home and the backup snapshots, with one qgroup over everything the workspace writes (see `specs/slice-fleet/spec.md`).

Non-goals, explicitly deferred:

- SEV-SNP and encrypted guest disks (a future generation; the qemu backend is the prerequisite, not the delivery).
- Guest-side `PerSourcePenalties` (becomes possible because DNAT preserves client source IPs, but is not enabled in this work).
- Falco or other tier-2 runtime-security agents on boxes (revisit after the tier-1 telemetry is baselined).
- Management-plane lockdown backport to gen-1 boxes (they are left untouched until turnover).
- A synthetic-abuse release test (detection is verified manually during canary; automated coverage stops at unit/snapshot tests).
- Account-level abuse response beyond the runbook (user suspension already exists, `specs/user-suspension.md`).
- Any change to the local desktop Lima mode or `mngr_lima` itself: lima remains the desktop-VM machinery (macOS/vz, trixie guests via the DWT pin); only the imbue_cloud slice backend leaves it.

## Expected behavior

User-visible behavior:

- A workspace on a gen-2 box behaves identically to today: same address contract (box IP + VM-root port + container port), same lease/adopt/stop/start flows, same desktop client.
- Migration off a gen-1 box appears as a normal stop/restore cycle: the workspace stops, and the next open (user-initiated or the client's automatic restart) restores it onto a gen-2 box.
  No notice machinery; the stopped-then-restoring UX is the same one stop/start and suspension already produce.
- A migrated workspace comes back with its VM dist-upgraded to trixie and its VM-level components (docker, owner-exec, latchkey, helpers) re-provisioned to current pins.
  If the upgrade fails repeatedly, the workspace stays stopped with the error recorded and an operator alerted; it is never handed back half-upgraded (strict mode, no bookworm-on-gen-2 fallback).
- A workspace generating abusive traffic volumes hits the connection ceilings (new connections throttled, not the VM killed) and shares bandwidth fairly with co-tenants; direct-to-MX email (outbound port 25) and spoofed-source packets are dropped outright, while authenticated mail submission (587/465) works normally. Normal workspaces never notice any of this.
- A workspace can still reach its own published service via the box's public address (hairpin to the slice port range stays allowed); it can no longer reach the box's management ports or other tenants' VMs at all.

Operator-visible behavior:

- `minds-admin server order` / `setup` gain gen-2 support: `debian13_64` reinstall, a custom partition layout with an XFS storage partition, and the gen-2 prep (qemu stack, nftables, WireGuard, template unit, collector).
- `minds-admin server drain <id>` marks a box `draining` (excluded from bake, restore-in-place, and restore candidates) and force-stops its leased rows via the existing per-workspace stop.
- Operators SSH gen-2 boxes over WireGuard (`minds-admin wg config` emits the client config; a sync command pushes peer-list changes fleet-wide); the OVH rescue console and a Modal-sandbox bounce host (behind the same Modal Proxy) are the break-glass paths.
- `just audit-boxes`, `list-servers`, and the reconcile sweep understand both generations.
- Volumetric anomalies file GitHub issues in imbue-ai/mngr-internal (deduplicated, tier-labeled), with SMTP to infra@imbue.com as the secondary channel; the abuse-response runbook says what to do when one fires.

System behavior:

- The connector dispatches every box-side operation (teardown, reconcile, stop/start scripts, capacity counting) on the row's generation; lease and release are externally unchanged.
- Restore candidate selection is generation-aware: gen-1 artifacts restore onto gen-2 boxes through the conversion path; gen-2 artifacts never restore onto gen-1 boxes.
- The connector's outbound SSH rides a Modal Proxy (static egress IPs); analytics collection and user SSH are unaffected (they use the public per-slice ports, which remain open).
- Boxes report per-tap interface metrics and per-VM nftables counters into the tier's OpenObserve; declared-vs-negotiated link speed drift raises an audit alert.

## Implementation plan

### DB schema (apps/remote_service_connector/migrations/)

- New migration: `box_generation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` on `bare_metal_servers`; same column on `pool_hosts`, stamped at bake and restore.
- Same migration (or sibling): `uplink_mbps INTEGER` on `bare_metal_servers` (declared per plan-code at registration; the HTB source of truth), `wg_address TEXT` (the box's WireGuard overlay IP, assigned at prep), and -- migration 032 -- `wg_public_key TEXT` (the box's WireGuard public key, generated on-box at prep and read back; operator client configs pin each box peer by it).
- `draining` joins the box status vocabulary (`ready` -> `draining` -> repave); bake, restore-in-place, and candidate listing all exclude it.
  `minds-admin server drain` additionally DESTROYS the box's unleased pool rows before force-stopping the leased ones: the connector's lease selects rows (not boxes), so an available row on a draining box would otherwise still be handed out.
- Migration-upgrade bookkeeping uses the existing `pool_hosts.attributes` JSONB (e.g. `guest_upgrade_failed`) -- no new column; with strict-mode upgrades the gen-2 fleet is uniformly trixie by construction.

### Qemu slice backend (libs/mngr_imbue_cloud/imbue/mngr_imbue_cloud/slices/)

- `qemu_slice.py` (new): the pure renderers. (Since cutover phase 3 the cloud-init material, the per-slice env file, and the destroy / listing commands live in the shared `libs/mngr_imbue_cloud/.../slices/gen2_scripts/` subpackage, which also ships into the connector container; `qemu_slice.py` keeps the unit / helper / sudoers, the slice DHCP server's config, unit and udp/67 policy, and the carve reserve script.)
  - One-time cloud-init NoCloud material: `user-data` (root + pool keys, per-slice user), `meta-data` (stable instance-id), `network-config` (placement-free `dhcp4: true` on the single virtio NIC, matched by driver; the box's dnsmasq hands out the /30 address, the gateway and the public resolvers 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8, see the restore bullet below).
  - The qemu invocation: `-nodefaults -no-user-config`, `-machine q35,accel=kvm,usb=off,smm=off` with S3/S4 disabled, `-cpu host,vmx=off,svm=off`, OVMF code-only pflash, virtio-blk boot disk, virtio datadisk, the cidata ISO as a read-only virtio-blk disk, virtio-net on the pre-created tap, QMP socket, the guest console on stdout (journald), `-sandbox on,obsolete=deny,elevateprivileges=deny,spawn=deny,resourcecontrol=deny` (valid because systemd runs qemu with no `-daemonize`; the sandbox/daemonize conflict is spike-verified). The exact argv is `render_slice_unit_file`'s snapshot test.
  - The reserve script: under the box-wide flock, checks slot capacity (gen-2 layout aware), picks the two host ports and the slice ordinal (which determines the /30 and tap name), verifies real free space on the storage filesystem covers the slice's full virtual size plus margin (the carve-time df guard), reflink-copies the staged base image (`cp --reflink=auto`), creates the datadisk, writes the per-slice directory (cidata ISO, env file with ports/IP/user), hands the pre-created per-slice unix user its disk files (prep creates all the users up front so `User=mngr-slice-%i` always resolves; the files stay group-readable by the slice service user, `slicehost`, so the stop/start transfer scripts can stream them), and enables the unit -- without booting.
  - Per-VM nftables rules rendered into the net-setup step: DNAT `box:<vm_port> -> <vm_ip>:22` and `box:<container_port> -> <vm_ip>:2222`, masquerade (plus `route_localnet` and a local-source masquerade on the tap, so the box's own loopback-addressed connections to the forwarded ports -- the image-cache transfer path -- hairpin into the VM), the guest-to-box input block (established/related replies to box-initiated connections, the guest's DHCP requests to the box's DHCP server on its tap, and ICMP diagnostics pass; everything else -- including the management sshd -- is dropped), the anti-spoofing drop (tap ingress must carry the VM's own address; first among the forward rules) and the direct-to-MX SMTP block (TCP 25 dropped into the per-VM `smtp_blocked` counter; 587/465 open), inter-VM block, hairpin-allow to the slice port range, named counters (bytes, packets, new connections, blocked SMTP attempts), the concurrent-connection ceiling (50,000) and sustained new-connection limit (300/s, throttling not killing), and the per-VM tc HTB class (guarantee ~`uplink_mbps`/slots, ceil `uplink_mbps`).
- `qemu_slice_client.py` (new): `QemuSliceVpsClient(VpsClientInterface)`, the drop-in sibling of `LimaSliceVpsClient` -- same SSH-command shape, driving the rendered scripts and `sudo systemctl start/stop mngr-slice@<name>` as the slice service user (`slicehost`; gen-2 boxes never carry the gen-1 `limahost` user, and a re-prep of a box that predates the rename removes it).
  Implements `provision_slice_vm`, `destroy_instance`, `list_instance_names`, disk/dir listing, `get_instance_status` (via systemd state), box health reads.
- `bare_metal.py`: gen-aware naming and constants (slice dir layout, tap/user naming from the ordinal, guest image path for the trixie base); existing lima constants untouched.
- `providers/slice_provider.py`, `providers/rebuild.py`: select the VPS client by the box's `box_generation` (threaded through the bake config and the lease response); no other provider changes -- the vps_docker bake sees the same VPS-parity surface.
- `wire_types.py`: additive `box_generation` field on the lease/workspace wire models (WireModel rules, default 1 against an older connector); the connector returns it on `POST /hosts/lease` and the `GET /workspaces` responses from the row's column, and restores restamp the column.
  This became possible mid-phase-2: the pre-tolerant strict client snapshot (`compat/wire_models_minds_0_3_16.py`, `extra="forbid"`) was pruned early (2026-08-23) because effectively the whole fleet runs 0.4.1+, whose tolerant models accept additive response fields.
- Adoption (`providers/adoption.py`) is unchanged: gen-2 VMs never replay cloud-init (true again since imbue-ai/mngr-internal#849 moved guest addressing to DHCP; between phase 2 and #849 a cross-placement restore replayed it once, see below), so the reconciler simply has nothing to heal, but rotation and pinning still apply to both generations. The gen-2 contract is: cloud-init runs once at first boot; the host key is written once at bake and replaced once at adoption; the network is DHCP.

### Systemd and box-installed artifacts (rendered by prep; the only box-installed pieces)

- `mngr-slice@.service` template unit: `User=` the per-slice user, `ExecStartPre=+` the root helper's `setup` verb (disk-media ownership, the unit's cgroup resource properties from the machine's size, tap create/attach, per-VM nftables chain, HTB class), `ExecStart` qemu under the systemd sandbox directives from the hardening decision above, `ExecStop` QMP `system_powerdown` with timeout, `ExecStopPost=+` net-teardown, `WantedBy=multi-user.target` (which is the whole boot-autostart story -- the gen-1 autostart script has no gen-2 equivalent).
- The net-setup/net-teardown script, the scoped sudoers entries (`slicehost` may run `systemctl start/stop/enable/disable/reset-failed` on exactly the per-ordinal slice units, one exact-argument command spec per ordinal -- no wildcard, since a sudoers `*` matches across whitespace and would grant every unit on the box), the slice DHCP server's dnsmasq config, unit and udp/67 policy (`/etc/mngr/slice-dhcp.conf` + `mngr-slice-dhcp.service` + `/etc/nftables.d/mngr-slice-dhcp.nft`: DHCP only, bound to the `mslice*` taps, one single-address range per ordinal, answered by broadcast with no ICMP probing; the unit runs dnsmasq as the unprivileged `mngr-dhcp` user under the slice unit's sandbox set holding only `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`, and the policy -- its own `inet mngr_slice_dhcp` table, boot-persistent like the lockdown's -- drops udp/67 off every interface but the taps; the slice units `Wants=` it), and the wg config.
  Prep converges each on content (compared byte-for-byte against the installed copy), so an unchanged re-prep touches nothing and a bumped renderer reaches existing boxes on the next prep; skew is benign (a box keeps its rules until re-prepped).

### Box prep and ordering (apps/minds_admin/)

- `slices/bare_metal_prep.py`: `build_gen2_box_prep_script` alongside the gen-1 builder (`server prep` / `setup` dispatch on the row's `box_generation`).
  Installs qemu/OVMF/nftables/genisoimage/dnsmasq-base/wireguard-tools/xfsprogs, verifies the pinned OVMF pflash path exists (fails loudly if trixie moved it), creates the `slicehost` service user plus the 512 pre-created per-slice users, creates the `mngr-dhcp` DHCP service user, installs the plugin-rendered prep artifacts (template unit / root helper / sudoers / the slice DHCP server's config, unit and udp/67 policy) content-converged (`cmp` + `visudo -c` + `dnsmasq --test`, `daemon-reload` on a changed unit, the DHCP server restarted only when its config or unit changed, the policy loaded with `nft -f` before the server starts), verifies the XFS storage partition is mounted at the storage root (fail otherwise; the gen-2 reinstall's custom layout provisions it), stages the trixie guest image (`DEFAULT_GEN2_SLICE_GUEST_IMAGE_URL`, an explicit pinned constant cross-referencing DWT's `[providers.lima]` trixie pin, with a release-checklist line to bump both together), whose virt-customize docker pin derives its distro suffix from the image's own os-release (so the pinned engine core lands as `~debian.13~trixie`), keeps the swapfile/no-auto-reboot/transfer-tooling steps, brings up wg0, and applies (or, when unconfigured, removes) the `:22` lockdown.
  The counter collector + timer is phase 4.
- WireGuard specifics (`slices/management_plane.py`): the box generates its own keypair at prep (the private key never leaves the box); prep echoes the public key (`MNGR_WG_PUBLIC_KEY` marker) and the CLI stamps it on the row (`wg_public_key`, migration 032). Peers come from the tier's committed file; the interface restarts only when the rendered config changed, so re-preps and peer syncs never bounce live sessions.
- The `:22` lockdown lives in its own `inet mngr_mgmt` nftables table (never the slice helper's `mngr_slices`), scoped entirely to `tcp dport 22` (established/related first, then loopback / wg0 / the proxy IPs, then a counting drop; the wg port and slice port range ride the accept policy), boot-persistent via nftables.service + `/etc/nftables.d/` (prep neutralizes the distro conf's `flush ruleset`, which would wipe the live per-VM tables on a service restart). It is GATED on the tier's `[modal_proxy]` config: without allowlisted proxy IPs the connector would be locked out of every workspace, so an unconfigured tier converges the box to open -- which is also the rollback path.
- `slices/ordering.py`: `GEN2_REINSTALL_OS_TEMPLATE = debian13_64` (the `setup` default for gen-2 rows). The custom partition scheme is automated: `build_gen2_reinstall_storage()` sends the reinstall a md-mirrored layout (`/boot` 1024MiB + ext4 root 102400MiB + fill-remaining XFS at the storage root; no swap partition, since prep provisions the mirrored swapfile and wipes raw swap partitions). The plan-code table's `uplink_mbps` column still waits for the first real gen-2 order.
- `cli/server.py`: gen-2 dispatch on setup/prep (register already carries `--box-generation` / `--uplink-mbps`); `server drain <id>` (sets `draining`, destroys unleased rows, force-stops leased rows via the connector admin stop, reports); `server repave <id>` remains future work (drain + `setup` compose it manually today).
- `cli/pool.py`: the bake reads the target box's generation and selects the backend; `--server-id` remains explicit.
- Per-tier `management_plane.toml` in `apps/minds/imbue/minds/config/envs/<tier>/` (loader + models in `imbue/minds/config`): `[[wireguard.operators]]` (name, PUBLIC key, overlay address) and `[modal_proxy]` (proxy name + static IPs) -- all public values, PR-reviewed. The dev tier commits a scaffold; a tier without the file simply has no management plane yet. (Since merged into each tier's `deploy.toml` as the optional `[management_plane]` table; the shape below is otherwise unchanged.)
- `minds-admin wg config`: emits the operator's client config from the boxes table (each prepped gen-2 box a peer at `<public_address>:51820`, `AllowedIPs` its `wg_address`/32, pinned by its recorded `wg_public_key`); `minds-admin wg sync-peers` converges the live fleet on the committed peer list (over `:22` before the lockdown, `--via-wg` after).
- Runbook: `apps/minds/docs/deploy/gen2-management-plane.md` (bring-up ordering, peer changes, rollback, break-glass: the OVH rescue console and a Modal-sandbox bounce host behind the same proxy).

### Connector (apps/remote_service_connector/)

- `box_scripts_gen2.py`: gen-2 variants of the upload/download/restore-reserve/stop/start/finalize scripts targeting the per-slice directory layout instead of `~/.lima`, dispatched by row generation; shared constants covered by the drift ratchet (below). (Superseded: cutover phase 3 moved the restore-reserve / download / in-place-resize renderers and the shared constants into the shared `libs/mngr_imbue_cloud/.../slices/gen2_scripts` subpackage, mounted into the connector container; `box_scripts_gen2.py` keeps only the connector's lifecycle command sequences and the upload script, and the drift ratchet is gone.)
  The gen-2 stop marker is the unit's `disable` (systemd `WantedBy` is the whole boot-autostart story), and the restore-reserve never enables the unit -- the download script enables + starts only once the disks have landed, so a box reboot can never boot a half-restored VM.
- **Restore cidata is copied verbatim from the artifact; the guest's address comes from the box by DHCP.** (Superseded 2026-09 by imbue-ai/mngr-internal#849, which replaced the phase-2 design below.)
  Phase 2 had the restore stamp a placement-keyed instance-id (`<instance>-g<generation>-o<ordinal>`) and regenerate a static `network-config` for the new ordinal, so cloud-init replayed once per placement change. That replay also reran the `ssh_keys` module (rewriting an adopted host key back to the bake-time key, healed later by the reconciler) and the `users` module (re-appending every bake-time root key), and would have stranded adopted VMs once phase 6 stops installing the reconciler.
  Now the box runs a DHCP server (dnsmasq, DHCP only, bound to the `mslice*` taps; one single-address range per ordinal rendered from the same derivation as the anti-spoof and DNAT rules, leases keyed by the ordinal-derived MAC) and the guest's `network-config` is a placement-free `dhcp4: true` on its single virtio NIC. The restore copies the artifact's `user-data`, `meta-data` and `network-config` unchanged, so the instance-id never changes and cloud-init is consumed exactly once, on first boot; only the env file is re-rendered for the new ordinal and ports. The helper's tap input chain admits DHCP (udp 68 -> 67) ahead of its drop, and the slice units `Wants=` the DHCP unit so a rebooted box never starts a VM before it. The cutover migrate builds the same placement-free cidata for a transplanted VM.
- The migration-conversion path: for a gen-1 artifact restoring onto a gen-2 box, the reserve unpacks the qcow2 pair into the gen-2 layout with a minimal connector-authored conversion `user-data` (no `ssh_keys` section -- the connector never holds the VM host private key, and the persisted `/etc/ssh` key survives the replay; mounts the data disk at its original lima mount point + fstab; retires the lima guest agent).
  After the first boot, the start supervisor drives the strict guest upgrade over SSH to the VM root (the pool key is authorized there since bake; pinned to the row's recorded host key): a detached in-VM script rewrites apt sources bookworm -> trixie and `dist-upgrade`s (status-file polled like the transfers), then the SUPERVISOR issues the reboot (observing sshd go down so the pre-reboot system is never re-verified), waits for both forwarded sshd banners (the container banner doubles as the container-start verification), and checks the reported release is trixie.
  Re-running the remaining VM-level provisioning (owner-exec, latchkey, snapshot helper) is left to the client-side adoption/open flow, whose installers are idempotent and version-gated; the binaries themselves survive the dist-upgrade.
  Strict mode: any upgrade failure lands the row back on `stopped` with `transition_error` recorded, `attributes.guest_upgrade_failed` set, and an error-level log (reaching the tier's error tracker per the #555 escalation precedent); retries follow the existing watchdog backoff; no bookworm fallback boot.
- `stop_start.py`: generation-aware candidate selection (`draining` excluded via the `ready` filter; gen-mismatch exclusions -- gen-1 -> gen-2 allowed via conversion, gen-2 -> gen-1 refused), the conversion step wired into the start supervisor, restore-in-place refused on a draining origin box (the abandoned local VM is best-effort deleted once the forced restore lands elsewhere).
  A successful restore restamps the row's `box_generation` (column + the `attributes` copy) and clears `guest_upgrade_failed`.
- `hosts.py`: teardown and reconcile dispatch on generation (gen-2 teardown = the idempotent destroy script: unit stop + disable + reset-failed, ordinal-link and instance-dir removal -- nftables/tap cleanup rides the unit's `ExecStopPost`, and the pre-created per-slice users are permanent); reconcile lists gen-2 instance dirs where it lists lima instances today.
- `app.py`: the tier's Modal Proxy attached to EVERY connector function (web app, transition supervisors, crons), read at `modal deploy` time from `MINDS_CONNECTOR_MODAL_PROXY_NAME`, which `minds-admin env deploy` threads from the tier's `management_plane.toml` (empty/absent = no proxy, direct egress -- the per-tier gate, dev first).
- Drift ratchet in `test_project_ratchets.py` (or a dedicated drift test): the connector's copies of the shared gen-2 constants and command renderers are pinned byte-for-byte against `mngr_imbue_cloud`'s source, replacing today's mirrored-by-hand comments. (Superseded: cutover phase 3 replaced the connector's mirror and its drift ratchet with the shared `libs/mngr_imbue_cloud/.../slices/gen2_scripts` subpackage, mounted into the connector container.)

### Telemetry and alerting (apps/observability/ + minds_admin's box_telemetry.py; implemented in phase 4)

- Per-tap hostmetrics scraping is free (taps are ordinary `msliceN` interfaces the box otelcol's network scraper already covers); the Evidence dashboard prototype charts them per slice.
- The on-box collector (`minds_admin`'s `slices/box_telemetry.py`, a prep-installed python3 script on a 60s systemd timer): per-VM nftables counters via `nft -j list counters` (labeled with the ordinal AND the instance name read from the slice env file, i.e. the host id), the conntrack-pressure gauge, the declared-vs-`ethtool` link-speed audit, the prep-artifact integrity check, the qemu-children tripwire, and the management-plane auth-log scan -- all emitted as JSON journald lines the existing pipeline ships.
  Implementation shape (supersedes the sketch): every tier-1 condition is evaluated ON the box -- thresholds, allowlists, and counter deltas live in the PR-reviewed rendered script -- and alert-worthy conditions are emitted as `MNGR_BOX_SIGNAL <name>` marker lines (the shared vocabulary is `observability`'s `box_signals.py`), so the server-side OpenObserve rules are trivial substring matches and alert payloads carry no log content.
- Management-plane tier-1 monitoring rides the same collector, exploiting the fact that a gen-2 box's legitimate behavior is fully enumerable: auth-log checks (direct root logins and password logins always; non-wg/non-proxy sources and password attempts once the lockdown is configured -- before it, the open `:22`'s scan noise and legitimate laptop logins make them meaningless), sudo outside the scoped `systemctl` grants, an integrity check of the root-owned prep artifacts (unit, helper, sudoers, the slice DHCP server's config, unit and udp/67 policy, wg config -- hashed against a manifest prep records after installing them, so re-prep refreshes the expectation), and the qemu-children tripwire (a healthy qemu spawns nothing after boot).
  Tier-2 (Falco or similar) stays deferred until these are baselined.
- Alert provisioning: `observability provision-alerts` idempotently creates the per-tier OpenObserve templates, destinations, and one alert rule per signal (period 10 min, threshold 1 row, silence 4 h = the dedupe window) -- GitHub issue creation via direct webhook (PAT in a header; payload-free templates per the telemetry spec: alert name, stream, tier, trigger time, never rows; tier in the title), SMTP to infra@imbue.com as the optional second destination (requires instance-side SMTP config, not yet provisioned).
  The signal set: per-VM new-connection rate (sustained > half the enforced ceiling), blocked direct-to-MX SMTP attempts, sustained egress above half the declared uplink, conntrack pressure, link-speed drift, and the management-plane tier-1 signals (auth-log anomalies, sudo anomalies, prep-artifact drift, qemu child processes). Box-origin egress profiling and true baselines stay with pmacct (phase 8).
- pmacct (phase 8): installed from Debian packages, fed by a sampled nftables `log group` rule, aggregating per-VM per-destination records, JSON output tailed into the existing pipeline; ~30-day retention in an operator-only stream.

### Docs

- `apps/minds/docs/deploy/abuse-response.md`: the runbook -- what each alert means, how to inspect a VM's counters/flows, the enforcement/quarantine levers (including suspension), and the per-rule promotion process (a rule graduates from alert-only after a clean false-positive-free history; duration deliberately unspecified).
- `apps/minds/docs/deploy/gen2-turnover.md`: the operator runbook for seed orders, drain batches, repave, and verification; supersedes the relevant parts of the slice-hardening rollout pattern.
- Updates to `host-pool-setup.md`, `environments.md`, and the security model for the new networking, lockdown, and telemetry.

## Implementation phases

Each phase lands as one or more PRs and leaves the system working; phases 3 and 4 can proceed in parallel with 2.

1. **Qemu backend and networking (code only, no fleet impact).**
   `qemu_slice.py` renderers, `QemuSliceVpsClient`, the template unit/net-setup/sudoers content, per-slice users, cidata builders, the reserve script with the df guard, DB migration for `box_generation`/`uplink_mbps`/`wg_address`, provider dispatch by generation.
   Exit: a gen-2 bake works end to end against a hand-prepped dev box.
2. **Connector dual-generation support.**
   Gen-2 box_scripts variants, generation dispatch in stop_start/hosts, the `draining` status, the gen-1 -> gen-2 restore conversion with the strict dist-upgrade, the drift ratchet, wire-type additions.
   Exit: stop/start round-trips on gen-2, and a gen-1 artifact restores (converted + upgraded) onto a gen-2 box in dev.
3. **Management-plane lockdown machinery.**
   Gen-2 prep's nftables box policy and WireGuard bring-up, `management_plane.toml`, `minds-admin wg config` + peer sync, Modal Proxy attachment on the connector (dev tier first), the bounce-host runbook note.
   Exit: a dev gen-2 box is unreachable on `:22` except from the connector, and operators work over wg.
4. **Telemetry tier 1-2 and alerting.**
   Per-tap hostmetrics, the counter collector, the link-speed audit, OpenObserve alert rules, the GitHub-webhook destination prototype + SMTP fallback, first dashboards (extending the Evidence prototype's extract).
   Exit: per-VM counters visible per tier; a manually-triggered threshold breach files a deduplicated GitHub issue.
5. **Dev canary.**
   One dev box ordered or repaved as gen-2 through the real flows; full checklist: bake, lease, workspace use, stop/start round-trip, gen-1 artifact migration with upgrade, drain of a gen-1 dev box, detection signals verified by hand.
6. **CI split fleet.**
   One gen-2 box joins the CI tier alongside the existing gen-1 boxes; the remote-workspace release tests run against both generations for the remainder of the rollout.
7. **Staging, then production turnover.**
   Redeploy tier services; seed two gen-2 boxes per production region (one for staging); then per batch: `server drain` -> workspaces restore onto gen-2 -> `server repave` -> box rejoins as gen-2 capacity; retire old `available` rows promptly; staging rehearses the exact production sequence.
8. **Flows, enforcement promotion, runbook.**
   pmacct sampled flows, the abuse-response runbook, per-rule promotion of alert-only rules to enforcement as their histories come back clean.
9. **Cleanup.**
   After the last gen-1 box and the last gen-1 artifact are gone: delete `lima_slice*.py`, the gen-1 box_scripts variants, `key_repair.py`, the gen-1 prep/autostart machinery, and the lima-format restore path; shrink the adoption reconciler to rotation-only; sweep the `CLEANUP:` markers this work introduces.

## Testing strategy

- **Unit tests** for every pure renderer (cloud-init material, qemu argv, unit content, net-setup rules, reserve script) as inline snapshots, following the existing `box_scripts_test.py` / `lima_slice_test.py` patterns; the /30-and-tap derivation, capacity math with the XFS reserve, and generation dispatch get direct tests.
- **The drift ratchet** pins the connector's copies of shared gen-2 constants/renderers to the plugin's source, failing on any divergence. (Superseded: cutover phase 3 replaced the connector's mirror and its drift ratchet with the shared `libs/mngr_imbue_cloud/.../slices/gen2_scripts` subpackage, mounted into the connector container.)
- **Integration tests** for `QemuSliceVpsClient` against a mock SSH transport (marker parsing, error paths, idempotent teardown), and for stop_start's generation-aware candidate selection and conversion sequencing against the fake stores.
- **Wire compatibility**: the additive `box_generation` field goes through the existing golden compat test against vendored old-client snapshots.
- **Release tests**: the existing remote-workspace release suite runs against both CI-tier generations during the rollout (phase 6); the gen-1 -> gen-2 migration path gets a dedicated release test (stop on gen-1, restore-with-upgrade on gen-2, workspace healthy).
- **Manual canary verification** (phases 5 and 7): the full operator checklist including detection signals -- deliberately manual, no synthetic-abuse automated test.
- **Edge cases to cover in tests**: reserve racing (flock respected across generations on a hand-shared box is out of scope -- gen-2 boxes never carry gen-1 slices), df-guard refusal, upgrade failure landing on `stopped` with the flag and error recorded, restore refusal of gen-2 artifacts on gen-1 candidates, `draining` exclusion in every selection path, teardown idempotence after partial carves, and the connection-ceiling throttle shape (new connections dropped, established ones untouched).

## Open questions

- **The per-VM nftables/tc ruleset is reasoning-derived, not live-tested**: the phase-1 rules (DNAT scoping, established/related input exemption, `route_localnet` loopback hairpin, connection ceilings, HTB classes) were validated with `nft --check` and netfilter-semantics analysis, but have never run on a real gen-2 box.
  The phase-5 dev canary is the designated ground-truth check for the rendered ruleset and must exercise every path: external SSH via DNAT, box-local image-cache transfer over loopback, guest egress, hairpin to the slice port range, the guest-to-management block, and the ceilings.
- **OVMF firmware path on trixie** (RESOLVED, phase 3): confirmed live on the first gen-2 box (2026-08-23) -- trixie's ovmf ships ONLY the `_4M` builds, so the qemu invocation now pins `/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE_4M.fd` (`GEN2_OVMF_CODE_PATH`); the prep verifies the file exists right after installing ovmf, so any future packaging move fails the prep loudly.
- **Phase-1 deliberate deferrals** (recorded in `.reviewer/outputs/autofix/unfixed/` on the phase-1 branch; each is a later-phase deliverable, not a bug): `SliceProvisionResult.slice_ordinal` is produced but unread until phase 2 persists it; `providers/rebuild.py` hardcodes the lima client until phase 2's wire change carries the lease's generation; `sweep_ci_slices_on_box` stays gen-1-only until phase 6; the `GEN2_UNIT_PATH`/`GEN2_HELPER_PATH`/`GEN2_SUDOERS_PATH` constants are unread until the prep implementation consumes them; the lima/qemu client SSH-plumbing duplication persists until phase 9 deletes the lima client.
- **OVH partition template** (RESOLVED, phase 3): `debian13_64` accepts the custom scheme with an XFS storage partition -- verified against the live reinstall API (xfs in the template's filesystem set, custom partitioning allowed, softraid raidLevel 1, size 0 = fill remaining) and exercised with a real reinstall; `server setup` now sends the layout for gen-2 rows.
- **OpenObserve -> GitHub webhook** (RESOLVED, phase 4, by live execution on the dev tier): the destination shape works -- the dev instance's own HTTP client created a real issue in imbue-ai/mngr-internal via the destination-test endpoint (PAT in an `Authorization` header plus an explicit `User-Agent`, which GitHub requires and OpenObserve's client does not set). Dedupe = the alert's 4-hour silence window; the direct webhook cannot update an existing issue, so "update-not-spam" is bounded to one issue per signal per tier per window (SMTP is the fallback if that proves too spammy). Also verified live: journald entries flatten into `body_message` / `body_syslog_identifier` columns (there is no `body` string -- the rules' SQL was pinned accordingly), and the v2 alerts API refuses `SELECT *`, so the rules select explicit columns; the interval `frequency` field's unit is ambiguous (source says seconds, the live scheduler treated it as minutes), so the rules use an exact seconds-field cron schedule instead. The dev tier's stored destination carries a placeholder token; arming delivery means re-running `provision-alerts` with a dedicated issues-write PAT.
- **Modal Proxy in deployed shape**: verify the connector's paramiko traffic actually egresses via the proxy IPs (workspace-level attach vs per-function), and that the dev tier's single Team-plan proxy is shared cleanly across dev envs.
- **Upgrade duration budget**: the dist-upgrade + re-provision adds minutes to a migration restore; measure on the canary and set the supervisor timeout (phase 2 ships a 1-hour poll bound) accordingly.
- **The conversion's one-time replay and data-disk remount are reasoning-derived**: the conversion user-data (the lima-mount-point remount + fstab, the guest-agent retirement; since imbue-ai/mngr-internal#849 the transplanted VM's cidata is the same placement-free one a carve gets -- stable instance-id, DHCP `network-config` -- so no netplan overwrite is needed) and the in-VM dist-upgrade flow follow documented cloud-init/apt semantics but have never run against a real gen-1 disk on a gen-2 box; the phase-5 canary's migration checklist is their ground truth (host key byte-identical after conversion, container back up post-upgrade, `host_dir` symlink resolving).
- **Phase-2 deliberate deferrals**: `sweep_ci_slices_on_box` stays gen-1-only until phase 6; the gen-2 restore's df guard sizes from `disk_gb / slot_count` (a conservative approximation of the carve budget) rather than mirroring the plugin's sizing math into the connector.
- **pmacct sampling rate and NFLOG group layout**: pick during phase 8 with real traffic volumes in hand.
- **wg0 addressing plan** (RESOLVED, phase 3): each tier's overlay is `10.202.0.0/16` (disjoint from the `10.201.0.0/16` per-slice /30 range); operators occupy `10.202.0.0/24`, assigned by hand in the committed per-tier file; boxes are assigned sequentially from `10.202.1.1` at prep (lowest free across all recorded rows, skipping `.0`/`.255`) and stamped on the row. Tiers reuse the same numbers safely because each tier is its own isolated WireGuard network (own keys, own peer lists).
- **Debian 12 LTS horizon (~June 2028)**: with strict upgrade-at-migration the gen-2 fleet is uniformly trixie, but gen-1 boxes and their guests persist until turnover completes; the turnover schedule should finish well before the horizon, and the runbook should note it.
